title: Turkey, light or dark meat, stewed, skin not eaten

content.title: About
content.content: Stewed turkey is tender poultry meat cooked slowly in liquid. The recipe uses both light (breast) and dark (thigh) meat, with the skin removed before cooking, resulting in a lower‑fat dish.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Turkey is a traditional centerpiece for holiday meals in the United States and many European countries.
Stewing preserves most B‑vitamins, which are sensitive to high heat.
Turkey meat contains less saturated fat than beef but more protein.
Light meat (breast) is leaner, while dark meat (thigh) is richer in iron and zinc.
Removing the skin reduces the calorie content of the finished dish by about 30 %.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Stewed turkey provides a complete source of protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Skin‑less preparation and moderate use of dark meat make the dish suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Rich in iron and zinc
items.content: Dark meat especially supplies iron for hemoglobin and zinc for immune function.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Turkey contains niacin (B3), vitamin B6 and B12, which support energy metabolism.

items.title: Low glycemic impact
items.content: The dish does not cause a rapid spike in blood sugar, making it friendly for people with pre‑diabetes.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Undercooked turkey may harbor Salmonella; ensure the internal temperature reaches 165 °F (74 °C).

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to turkey proteins.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Adding salt or prepared broths can raise sodium levels; monitor seasoning.

items.title: Iron overload
items.content: People taking iron supplements should consider the additional iron from dark meat.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Stewed turkey can be served as a main course, sliced for salads, used in sandwiches, or added to soups and stews. It pairs well with herbs (rosemary, thyme), vegetables, and whole grains.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked stewed turkey in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portions for 2‑3 months. Reheat to 165 °F (74 °C) before serving.
